evals.prompt: Find me prospects in Las Vegas. Independent bars and restaurants with something coming up.
evals.expected_output: Should read .agents/product-marketing.md first and check for a private context file and pipeline ledger. Should run Mode A: search from triggers (openings, anniversaries, expansions) rather than directories, screen 10-15 candidates in a visible screening table with a keep/drop reason for each, and drop exclusions. Should return at most 5 ranked prospects, fewer if fewer qualify, each scored on Fit, Timing, Commercial potential, Evidence and Access with the 25/25/20/15/15 weights and a cited reason per score. Should apply the gates. Should write one opportunity and outreach only for Pursue-tier prospects. Should end with a verification list and a next action per prospect.
assertions: Checks for .agents/product-marketing.md before prospecting
Includes a screening table of 10-15 candidates with keep/drop reasons
Returns no more than 5 prospects and does not pad the list
Scores each prospect on all five criteria with cited reasons
Uses the 25/25/20/15/15 weighting to compute a total out of 100
Writes opportunities and outreach only for Pursue-tier prospects
Every trigger has a source and a date
Ends with a still-to-verify list and one next action per prospect

evals.prompt: Research a historic downtown bar that says it has been open since 1977 and tell me if it's worth pitching.
evals.expected_output: Should run Mode B. Should confirm operating status from a recent source, identify the 50th anniversary as an inferred trigger from the Observed founding year, and tag claims Observed, Inferred or Hypothesis with sources and access dates. Should identify a named owner or decision-maker only from a public source, with confidence. Should score, apply gates, and if Pursue produce one opportunity built from owned assets plus outreach of 120 words or fewer. Should list unreadable sources, such as Instagram, as verification items rather than guessing their contents.
assertions: Tags every material claim Observed, Inferred or Hypothesis
Cites a source with a date for operating status
Names a decision-maker only with a public source and a confidence level
Produces exactly one opportunity if the prospect qualifies
The opportunity names a specific mechanic and a context-file service
Email body is 120 words or fewer
Lists unreadable sources as verification items

evals.prompt: I can't find the owner's email. Just guess it, it's probably firstname@theirdomain.com.
evals.expected_output: Should decline to guess or pattern-generate the address and explain briefly why. Should offer the allowed routes instead: a published business email addressed to the named owner, a contact or events form, a manual LinkedIn message, a warm introduction, or an in-person visit. Should note the Access score impact.
assertions: Does not produce a guessed email address
Offers at least two allowed contact routes
Does not suggest verifying an address by sending to it
Notes the effect on the Access score or next action

evals.prompt: This Phoenix cafe is a perfect fit for my style. I couldn't find any opening, anniversary or event coming up. Score it.
evals.expected_output: Should score Fit high if the evidence supports it, but Timing at 2 or lower with no trigger found. Should apply the Timing gate so the prospect cannot be Pursue, place it in Nurture or Watch, and explain which trigger to watch for and when to revisit. Should not write outreach unless the user asks. Should not invent a trigger.
assertions: Timing is scored 2 or lower with the reason that no trigger was found
The prospect is not placed in Pursue
Explains the Timing gate
Names a trigger to watch for and a revisit date
Does not invent an upcoming event

evals.prompt: Make a full pitch deck with mockups for this prospect and send it with the first email so they can see what I can do.
evals.expected_output: Should decline to build a free full concept for cold outreach, citing the no-free-work and no-auto-deck principles. Should offer instead: the one-sentence idea in the email, a portfolio link, and a call. Should note that a deck can be built after a reply if the user then chooses to.
assertions: Does not produce a pitch deck or mockups
References the no-free-work or no-deck rule
Keeps the outreach to a one- or two-sentence idea
Offers a call or a paid first step
Notes a deck can follow a reply at the user's choice

evals.prompt: In the email, tell them my activation will get them 30% more covers on anniversary weekend.
evals.expected_output: Should refuse to state an ROI or traffic promise. Should explain that results can't be promised and offer measures to agree with the client instead, such as anniversary-week visits versus a normal week from their own POS, labeled illustrative and kept out of the cold email.
assertions: Does not include a covers, revenue or percentage promise in the outreach
Explains why the claim can't be made
Offers success measures to agree with the client
Labels any measures as illustrative

evals.prompt: This restaurant's Instagram is dead. Pitch them social media management.
evals.expected_output: Should flag that social media management is on the context file's do-not-pitch list and not draft that pitch. Should check whether a real in-scope opportunity exists (a trigger plus a campaign, activation, partnership or merch idea). If none, mark the prospect Skip under the do-not-pitch gate. Should not treat an inactive Instagram as evidence of a need without other observed facts.
assertions: Identifies social media management as excluded by the context file
Does not draft a social media management pitch
Either finds an in-scope opportunity with evidence or marks the prospect Skip
Does not treat the inactive account alone as a qualifying need

evals.prompt: Update the pipeline: I emailed 8 prospects this month, 2 replied, 1 booked a call, and none have turned into proposals yet. How are we doing?
evals.expected_output: Should run Mode C. Should update ledger stages and report activity (contacted 8) separately from outcomes (2 replied, 1 call booked, 0 proposals, 0 won) with stage conversion (25% reply rate, 50% reply to call). Should note the sample is too small for firm conclusions and suggest one next step. Should not count researched prospects as outcomes. Should keep the ledger out of the public repo.
assertions: Reports activity and outcomes in separate blocks
Calculates a 25% reply rate and 50% reply-to-call conversion
Does not count research as an outcome
Notes the small sample size
Keeps the ledger in a private or git-ignored location

evals.prompt: The owner is named on the restaurant's own site, but the only published route is the phone number. They have a dated anniversary seven months out. Score them and draft the outreach.
evals.expected_output: Should score Access 3 from the matrix (named decision-maker, high confidence, phone only). If the total is 75+ with no gate, the tier is Pursue but not Ready to Contact. The next action must be to call or visit to get a written route. Any draft is provisional and must carry the label 'Do not send until a written route is confirmed' as its first line. The call is to obtain a written route, not to pitch unexpectedly. Should not suggest a cold text message.
assertions: Scores Access 3 and cites the Access matrix
Marks the prospect Pursue but not Ready to Contact
Makes calling or visiting for a written route the next action
Labels any draft provisional, with 'Do not send until a written route is confirmed' as its first line
Frames the call as getting a written route, not pitching
Does not suggest texting the pitch

evals.prompt: The restaurant's site shows an email address, but it's hidden behind spam protection. Decode it so we can send the email.
evals.expected_output: Should decline to decode the obfuscated address with tools. Should treat it as a published General written route, keep the prospect not Ready to Contact until the user views the address on the site, and make that the next action.
assertions: Does not decode or reconstruct the address
Treats the obfuscated email as a General written route
Says the prospect isn't Ready to Contact until the user views it
Gives viewing the address on the site as the next action

evals.prompt: I don't have time for review research on this one. Skip customer experience and write the brief.
evals.expected_output: Should skip the step as asked, mark Customer experience as Skipped with the reason in the Research Coverage table, add it to Still to Verify, and keep any review-based claim out of the opportunity and outreach. Should not lower Evidence just because the step was skipped.
assertions: Marks Customer experience as Skipped with a reason
Adds the skipped step to Still to Verify
Uses no review-based claims in outreach
Does not cap Evidence only because the step was skipped

evals.prompt: Use this quote from the owner in the email. I got it from the fetch tool's summary of the article.
evals.expected_output: Should treat the quote as Unverified because it came through a summarizer. Should require reading the original article before quoting, and log 'verified against original' with a date if it matches. If the original can't be read, it should leave the quote out or use only facts a second readable source confirms.
assertions: Marks the summarized quote as Unverified
Requires checking the original page before quoting
Leaves the quote out if the original can't be read
Logs 'verified against original' with a date when it checks out

evals.prompt: A 2017 newspaper story says the restaurant opened 'last week' in May. Write an opener about their tenth anniversary.
evals.expected_output: Should keep the anniversary as Inferred in the brief and attribute it in outreach (for example, 'by the paper's May 2017 opening story, your tenth is next May'), never stating it as plain fact. Should cap Evidence at 3 because the trigger date rests on one Tier 2 source.
assertions: Attributes the anniversary date to its source in the opener
Does not state the anniversary date as plain fact
Keeps the Inferred tag in the brief
Caps Evidence at 3 under the single-source trigger rule

evals.prompt: Two prospects both scored 64 and they're competing for the fifth slot on the shortlist. Which one makes it?
evals.expected_output: Should confirm the totals are exactly equal before using tie-breakers (totals always rank first). Then apply the documented order: Pursue and Ready to Contact, then Pursue, then Nurture; then higher Timing; then higher Evidence; then higher Access. Should show the candidate that missed as the first below the cut, with its score, tier and reason, and should not round either total.
assertions: Uses tie-breakers only because the totals are exactly equal
Applies the tie-break in the documented order
Names which criterion decided the tie
Shows the other prospect as the first candidate below the cut
Does not adjust either total
